subject: Dedicated fleet congestion & customer prioritization request
messages:
From: Maria Chen <maria@scoutai.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-10T09:14:00Z
Subject: Dedicated fleet contention - ScoutAI production regression

Jonas,

We're seeing repeated tail-latency spikes and 503s in production since late last night. Our monitoring shows frequent preemption on the cluster backing our dedicated capacity (deal SCOUT-001). This started after a large onboarding batch for another customer was pushed into the same GPU pool.

Impact: 30% increase in p95 latency, failed inference calls affecting real-time features for paying customers. Our SREs have collected logs and a short postmortem — attaching errors log.

We have a signed reserved capacity contract and committed billing for the quarter. Can you confirm: 1) whether there was an emergency reallocation that affected our lanes, 2) what immediate mitigation you can apply, and 3) an ETA for a durable fix? ScoutAI is prepared to escalate contract remedies if this persists.

Immediate ask: an isolation or priority rule we can rely on during our morning traffic window (14:00-18:00 PT).

Attachments: scout_prod_errors.log (text)

Thanks,
Maria Chen
Head of ML Ops | ScoutAI
procurement@scoutai.com

--
On Fri, Oct 9, 2026 at 20:03 UTC, ScoutAI Deployment Alerts wrote:
> Alert: cluster-gpu-pool-7 detected >80% queue length for >15m
> Event ID: evt-20261009-2234

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Maria Chen <maria@scoutai.com>, procurement@scoutai.com
Date: 2026-10-10T11:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated fleet contention - ScoutAI production regression

Forwarding ScoutAI's incident to ops + deals team. TL;DR: SCOUT-001 is a committed reserved capacity customer (120 vGPU equivalent) with SLA windows. They report preemption and latency; they believe another onboarding job from a different deal consumed burst capacity in the same pool.

Proposed immediate actions (we should choose one within 2 hours):
- Option A: Enforce hard isolation for SCOUT-001 in cluster-gpu-pool-7 for their peak window (14:00-18:00 PT). This requires temporarily bumping other customers to overflow pools.
- Option B: Apply a soft-priority policy: throttle best-effort onboarding jobs in the pool during SCOUT's window and schedule a rolling backfill overnight.
- Option C: Move SCOUT's critical slices to a nearby warm node group (temporary dedicated nodes) for 24-48h while we rebalance.

Tradeoffs: A gives strongest isolation but risks disrupting onboarding SLAs for other customers and may trigger credits. B is minimally disruptive but may not restore p95 fully. C costs us short-term egress capacity and manual ops work but keeps other customers largely unaffected.

I attached a one-page proposal for priority rules (proposed_priority_rules.pdf). Please review and reply with your recommendation. If we agree, I'll notify ScoutAI with a remediation ETA and start the ops change.

Jonas
Director, Deals & Capacity Strategy
Redwood Inference
Attachments: proposed_priority_rules.pdf (1 page)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-10T12:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated fleet contention - ScoutAI production regression

+1 to Option C with a short-term cap. Notes:
- Ops can stand up 6 warm nodes in cluster-gpu-pool-7 within 3 hours if we approve. That will remove preemption for SCOUT slices.
- I'll add a temporary per-deal concurrency cap for the onboarding job that caused the contention; we should throttle it to 30% of its requested burst for 48h.
- Recommend we include a clause for future onboarding bursts: max-burst parameter tied to reserved capacity tier. I'll update the matrix.

I updated the live spreadsheet with the node delta and estimated cost. Link: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/priority_matrix_v1.xlsx

—Ben
Sr. Capacity Planner, Redwood

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Maria Chen <maria@scoutai.com>, procurement@scoutai.com
Date: 2026-10-12T10:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated fleet contention - ScoutAI production regression

Thanks team — decision: implement Option C (temporary warm nodes) plus immediate throttle on the offending onboarding job.

Plan and comms:
- Ops to provision 6 warm nodes for SCOUT-001 in cluster-gpu-pool-7 within 3 hours of this email.
- Ben to enforce the 30% throttle on the onboarding job until 2026-10-14 23:59 PT.
- Jonas to notify ScoutAI with a remediation ETA and an apology note; offer one day of service credit if p95 remains > target after remediation.
- Karthik, please work with runtime team to add a short-term scheduling knob (burst_cap_per_deal) as a follow-up engineering ticket.

I've attached the priority matrix we'll use to formalize this rule set. We'll iterate it into the customer SLA annex for future reserved deals.

Attachments: priority_matrix_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success & Capacity Operations
Redwood Inference
